newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-RBA sees core inflation around current levels.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-RBA sees core inflation around current levels.

text.p: Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) governor Ian Macfarlane said on Thursday he saw the underlying inflation rate staying around the current level of 2.1 percent in the foreseeable future.
"We expect it will continue at something like that for the foreseeable," Macfarlane told a derivatives.
Macfarlane said he did not believe Australia had received the recognition it deserved for improving its inflation performance.

Australia's inflation rate had averaged 2.8 percent over the 1990s, compared with 3.8 percent for the OECD as a whole, and had been lower than traditionally low inflation countries like Germany and Switzerland, he said.
"I think that Australia has actually been slow to receive the recognition that it deserves for its monetary policy framework and for the inflation performance that now prevails."
Macfarlane said the recent inflation performance was not a flash in the pan.
He said the economy remained free of major macro-economic imbalances.
"At the moment looking ahead, we can see there's a fair chance of achieving the sort of sustainable growth that we achieved through the 1950s and 1960s," he said.
